rationale_overall: This week's pool was dominated by noise that had to be filtered out: Iran nuclear/missile diplomacy headlines (no listed ticker), a Sri Lankan rocket-launcher weapons cache (LTTE ordnance, not a company), a 'Rocket League' video-game promo and an iHeartRadio station literally named 'The Rocket' (keyword false-matches), routine ISS Crew-12 astronaut-arrival stories repeated across five outlets (no new commercial catalyst), a Chinese lunar rocket/capsule test (foreign, non-investable), and niche GNSS/satellite items involving private or foreign entities (Divirod/OKI, Safran-Syntony). The substantive AI-wave coverage (Meta's $10B Indiana data center, Vertiv order book, Micron rally, Magnificent Seven capex, Nvidia/Tower optical modules) and the nuclear-comeback op-ed all reinforce theses already expressed via NVDA, GOOGL and SMR rather than pointing to a new vehicle. Rocket Lab (RKLB) drew a bull-case piece and a DIU hypersonic-test mention, both supportive of the existing holding, not a reason to swap. General Dynamics' Iraq contract win and a junior uranium driller (Homeland Uranium Corp., likely thin/OTC) were considered as defense/nuclear add candidates but neither offered a clearly stronger early-wave catalyst than what's already held, and the uranium name fails the liquidity guardrail. No genuine new-wave catalyst rose above the bar for a swap this week, so the managed watchlist is left unchanged with GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB and SMR intact alongside the SPY anchor.
